knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,2 xy,\,x + y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=2 xy + x + y$ for $1\le x\le 5$ and $-2\le y\le 5$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a negative $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{-2}^{5}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2 uv + u + v⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):1\le u\le 5,\ -2\le v\le 5\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,2 v + 1⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,2 u + 1⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 v + 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 u + 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨- 2 v - 1,\,- 2 u - 1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $k$-component has the opposite sign to the requested orientation. Reverse the entire vector:

$$
\mathbf N=-\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨2 v + 1,\,2 u + 1,\,-1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(2 uv + u + v) \\ &=2 uv + u + v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (u)(v) \\ &=2 uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(u) + (v) \\ &=u + v.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(2 uv + u + v)(2 v + 1) \\ &=4 uv^{2} + 4 uv + u + 2 v^{2} + v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(2 uv)(2 u + 1) \\ &=4 u^{2} v + 2 uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(u + v)(-1) \\ &=- u - v.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=4 u^{2} v + 4 uv^{2} + 6 uv + 2 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{-2}^{5}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $4 u^{2} v + 4 uv^{2} + 6 uv + 2 v^{2}$.

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨2 z,\,xy,\,x + y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=- xy - x + y$ for $1\le x\le 3$ and $-2\le y\le 4$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a positive $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{4}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- uv - u + v⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):1\le u\le 3,\ -2\le v\le 4\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,- v - 1⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,1 - u⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & - v - 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 - u\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨v + 1,\,u - 1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product already has the requested orientation, so

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨v + 1,\,u - 1,\,1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (- uv - u + v) \\ &=- 2 uv - 2 u + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(u)(v) \\ &=uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(u) + (v) \\ &=u + v.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(- 2 uv - 2 u + 2 v)(v + 1) \\ &=- 2 uv^{2} - 4 uv - 2 u + 2 v^{2} + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(uv)(u - 1) \\ &=u^{2} v - uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(u + v)(1) \\ &=u + v.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=u^{2} v - 2 uv^{2} - 5 uv - u + 2 v^{2} + 3 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{4}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $u^{2} v - 2 uv^{2} - 5 uv - u + 2 v^{2} + 3 v$.

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,2 xy,\,x + y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=- 2 xy + x + y$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 3$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a negative $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- 2 uv + u + v⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):-1\le u\le 2,\ -1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,1 - 2 v⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,1 - 2 u⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 - 2 v \\ 0 & 1 & 1 - 2 u\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨2 v - 1,\,2 u - 1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $k$-component has the opposite sign to the requested orientation. Reverse the entire vector:

$$
\mathbf N=-\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨1 - 2 v,\,1 - 2 u,\,-1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(- 2 uv + u + v) \\ &=- 2 uv + u + v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (u)(v) \\ &=2 uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(u) + (v) \\ &=u + v.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(- 2 uv + u + v)(1 - 2 v) \\ &=4 uv^{2} - 4 uv + u - 2 v^{2} + v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(2 uv)(1 - 2 u) \\ &=- 4 u^{2} v + 2 uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(u + v)(-1) \\ &=- u - v.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=- 4 u^{2} v + 4 uv^{2} - 2 uv - 2 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $- 4 u^{2} v + 4 uv^{2} - 2 uv - 2 v^{2}$.
